q: The goal of a successful trader is to make the best trades. Money is secondary.
Risk comes from not knowing what you are doing.
The market can stay irrational longer than you can stay solvent.
Cut your losses short and let your winners run.
Plan the trade, trade the plan.
Amateurs think about how much they can make. Professionals think about how much they can lose.
A losing trade that followed your rules is a good trade.
No setup is also a position. Waiting is part of the job.
Protect your capital first. Opportunity returns; lost capital may not.
Your edge only shows up over many trades. Judge the process, not one result.
The urge to win it back is the most expensive emotion in trading.
Small, repeatable risk beats occasional heroics.
Let price come to your level. Chasing is paying for impatience.
Write the stop before you enter. Decide the loss while you are calm.
Boredom is not a signal. Neither is fear of missing out.
Consistency is a hundred ordinary days, not one extraordinary one.
